profile_text.body:
The Alan Turing Institute is a nonprofit based in London, United Kingdom, also known as the Turing Institute. Its site describes its mission as changing the world using data science and artificial intelligence, and it says it works with a wide range of partners across government, industry and academia to deliver that mission. It runs events and publishes Turing News, and it points readers to CETaS and to Skills at the Turing.

The site highlights several research efforts. The Defence AI Research Centre (DARe) is described as providing strategic advantage for UK Defence and National Security through targeted development of novel AI technologies, in partnership with government, industry and academia. Other work named on the site includes Project Bluebird, where a researcher named Amy works on ways AI systems can benefit air traffic control, such as digital twins of UK airspace to forecast aircraft behaviour and trajectories, and Aemelia, described as AI-enabled satellite morphological inference from multidimensional inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) data. The site also mentions open-source infrastructure for argument-based AI assurance, helping teams build, evidence and maintain structured arguments that their AI systems are trustworthy and ethical, and research on AI forecasting combined with expert knowledge and real-world climate context to extend the range of predictions.

The site profiles individual researchers: Isabel Fenton, who applies data science and AI to environmental challenges such as biodiversity loss and renewable energy generation, and Carlos Gavidia-Calderon, a research software engineer whose work the site describes as spanning the ethics of machine learning to digital twins of hearts. No products, lawsuits or MCP servers are recorded for the institute.
